title: Entanglement entropy of fermions in a strange metal
authors: Santanu Singh, Surajit Bera, Chenyuan Li, Subir Sachdev, Sumilan Banerjee
abstract: The subsystem-size dependence of ground-state entanglement entropy and its crossover to thermal entropy as a function of temperature are well understood for one-dimensional (1D) gapless systems described by conformal field theory (CFT), and for free fermions with a Fermi surface in any dimension. However, little is known about the entanglement entropy for gapless fermionic systems without quasi-particles, such as a strange metal. Here we study the entanglement entropy of fermions in a solvable large-$N$ 1D lattice model akin to the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (Yukawa SYK) model. In this model, two Fermi points are coupled to scalar bosons via spatially random Yukawa interactions, providing a solvable model of a strange metal when the bosons become critical at a quantum critical point. We exactly compute the second Rényi entropy of fermions in a spatial subregion in this model. Our results unravel crucial role of intra-subregion entanglement between fermionic and bosonic degrees of freedom along with the inter-subregion entanglement in understanding the ground states of such strongly coupled fermion-boson systems. We show that the crossover from thermal entropy to entanglement entropy, is captured by a single scaling ansatz, that collapses the second Rényi entropy of fermions for different subregion sizes and temperatures into a single universal curve. We further show that the universal scaling curve for the critical strange metal is well described by the standard CFT formula, albeit with an effective central charge substantially larger than the non-interacting value.
summary: This paper investigates the entanglement entropy in strange metals using a solvable large-N model akin to Yukawa SYK. By calculating the second Rényi entropy, the authors show that the crossover between thermal and entanglement regimes follows universal scaling laws predicted by CFT theory. This confirms strong quantum correlations beyond simple Fermi liquid descriptions.
main_problem: The study addresses the entanglement entropy of gapless fermionic systems, specifically those exhibiting strange metal behavior without well-defined quasiparticles.
main_result: The crossover from thermal to entanglement entropy is captured by a single universal scaling ansatz, and for the critical strange metal, this curve follows the CFT form with an effective central charge larger than non-interacting values.
method: The authors employ large-N field theory techniques, exactly computing the second Rényi entropy via imaginary-time path integrals and solving resulting saddle-point equations.
model_or_system: The model is a solvable 1D lattice system analogous to the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (Yukawa SYK) model, coupling two Fermi points to scalar bosons via random Yukawa interactions.
key_observables: Second Rényi entropy of fermions ($S^{(2)}_A$), effective central charge ($c_{	ext{eff}}$), and the temperature/size dependence of entanglement entropy.
important_parameters: The system behavior is controlled by a parameter $\gamma$, defining regimes: Strange Metal (QCP, $\gamma = \gamma_c$), Ordered Phase ($\gamma < \gamma_c$), and Fermi Liquid (FL) Phase ($\gamma > \gamma_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the large-$N$ limit. The study also uses specific path integral formalisms and numerical techniques like recursive Green's function inversion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup, a phase diagram showing the QCP separating FL from Strange Metal regimes, and plots demonstrating the scaling collapse of $S^{(2)}_A$ using CFT-like formulas.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the physical problem (entanglement in strange metals), then detailing the mathematical machinery (large-$N$ saddle points, path integrals), presenting results across different temperature/size regimes, and finally deriving universal scaling laws.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the study of entanglement entropy scaling laws and critical behavior provides theoretical tools applicable to understanding quantum criticality in strongly interacting many-body systems relevant to AMO physics.
